newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares seen up on politics, profits.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares seen up on politics, profits.

text.p: Istanbul stocks are expected to maintain an upward bias on political stability and company profit expectations, brokers said on Friday.

"It has been understood that pessimistic expectations would not turn to reality. There will not be any currency crisis, interest rates will not boom, the Treasury is able to borrow for longer maturities," said Suhan Seckin, general manager at Toros securities.

The IMKB-100 index, which has gained 26.2 percent since September 13, leapt 2.54 percent to a new record close of 81,743.62 on Friday after being boosted by Wednesday's rejection of a censure motion against the Islamist-led government.
"We knew that positive developments in money markets in early September would have a positive reflection on the stock market," said Turgay Ozaner, manager at Global securities.

The Treasury was successful in launching three-year foreign currency-denominated bonds by selling $1.12 billion of them to Turkish banks in mid-September as part of the government's two revenue raising packages unveiled since July.
The government plans to raise $2 billion more via similar bond issues by the end of 1996.
"If a second issue also meets demand, then the index's rise will accelerate," Ozaner said.
Semih Cetin, general manager of Bayindir securities, said rejection of the censure motion rejection eased political tension and inspired the government to achieve its economic targets.
"The markets have been receiving messages from government sources that interest rates would fall gradually by restricting spending in the planned zero-deficit 1997 budget," he said.
Turkey's 1997 draft budget and economic targets, unveiled by the Finance Minister on Friday, were criticised as unrealistic by the opposition parties, economists and businessmen.
"When the goverment comes with a zero-deficit budget, then privatisation must definitely be on its agenda, Seckin said.

Turkey plans to speed up its 10-year-old sluggish sell-off programme with new tenders to be opened this year. State-owned Etibank will be the first, to be followed by flat steel maker Eregli Demir Celik Fabrikalari, as recently outlined by the privatisation body OIB.
"After the index hits one dollar, privatisation hopes will drive the stock market," said Ozaner from Global.
The index, targeting 84,000-85,000 and eventually $1 after breaching the critical 80,000 mark today, currently stands at $0.86 in dollar terms, down from a high of one dollar in April.

"The thought that a selloff spree will start caused the index to breach 80,000 level. Government announcements are gaining importance for the coming days. The index may go up to 100,000 level in the medium-term," said Cetin from Bayindir.
